input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: § 7.2 imposes an open-ended reverse MFN on us: we would have to disclose any more favourable third-party offer and match it for Vendor before engaging another provider. That is the wrong direction (MFN burdening Customer) and is effectively the walk-away position under the rule — an unlimited obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor, with no product scope, time limit, or comparison carve-outs. It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred remedy is deletion; no Vendor-granted MFN in our favour exists elsewhere in the document, so nothing beneficial is lost.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted § 7.2 because it reverses the usual position by requiring us to disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit, which our playbook does not accept; this also aligns with § 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Delete the reverse MFN obligation in § 7.2
